author: Kai Moreno
title: SSH bastion key rotation for Private deployments
content:
# Purpose
Private customers rotate the SSH keys that open their bastion to Redwood support. This is not a Hosted API key and it is never disabled from Console.

# When to use
The customer mentions bastion, jump host, SSH, or 'the key we gave your on-call'. They are not talking about a Console API token named prod-web or prod-backend.

# Steps
1) Customer generates a new ed25519 key on their side.
2) They add it to the bastion allow-list.
3) They tell Private Deployments the new fingerprint.
4) They remove the old fingerprint after we confirm login.
Support does not disable anything in Console.

# Priority and routing
Planned bastion rotations are P4 and stay with Support. Broken bastion access that blocks a Sev0 is P1 and goes to Private Deployments. Never add security-incident for a planned bastion rotation.

# Guardrails
Never ask them to paste a private key. Never disable a Hosted API key because someone said 'rotate the key' on a Private ticket.

# Related
Private access runbook. This page does not cover Hosted API tokens.
